b) Equipment
which may come into contact with flammable fluids or vapours and which under fault conditions may produce arcs, electrical sparks, friction sparks nor hot surfaces, shall be designed and installed to reduce to an acceptable minimum the overall risk of a fault occurring that will ignite the flammable vapours. In designing the air supply system for forced air ventilated equipment, the possibility of contamination of the air by flammable vapours shall be taken into account. If the equipment and its ducting, including joints, are in an area which can be so contaminated, they shall be capable of meeting the conditions appropriate to the environment. for Category A equipment shall consider the design requirements of flange and hole dimensions or other equivalent means, such as flame traps for adequate safety from flame propagation. 6. Environment

6.1 Environment I - Environment I is an atmosphere in a space in which uncovered flammable fluids or vapours exist, or can exist either continuously or intermittently (for example, in fuel tanks or within fuel systems 1. 5.2 Environment I/ - Environment II is an atmosphere m which flammable mixtures occur only as a result of a fault causing spillage or leakage, and where an explosive occur. can be expected to environment may

Environment III is an atmosphere where the probability of flammable mixtures 5.3 Environment HIarising from aircraft systems is sufficiently IOW to be disregarded, for example, within passenger cabins and well-ventilated areas not containing flammable fluids. 5.4 Environment 6. Explosion IV Environment IV is an atmosphere within a designated fire cone.

8. Acceptance 8.1 Category Test A Tests of test Procedure

8.1 .I

Preparation

a) Preparation of Test Case or Enclosure - When necessary, the test case or enclosure shall be prepared for explosion-proof testing by drilling and tapping openings in the case or enclosure for inlet~and outlet hose connections to the fuel-vaprjur air mixture circulation system and for mounting a spark gap device. The case volume shall not be altered by more than f5 percent by any modification to facilitate the introduction of explosive vapour. b) Hose Installation to prevent ignition supply~hose. When inserting a hose from a blower, adequate of the ambient mixture by backfire or the release the explosive may be drilled internally. precaution shall be taken or pressure through the mixture within the case or and tapped for the spark

c) Spark Gap Device - A spark gap device for igniting enclosure shall be provided. The case or enclosure gap device or the spark gap device may be mounted

d) Case Installation - The case or encloure with either the test item or a model of the test end of the same volume and configuration in position within the case or enclosure shall be connected and oriented in the explosion chamber mechanically and electrically, as recommended by the manufacturer for normal service installation. This shall include any cooling provisions as necessary to perform the tests described in 8.1.2. 8.1.2 Performance 1of test The test shall be performed three times as follows:

Step

The chamber shall ambient pressures The ambientzhamber the chamber shall

be sealed and the internal pressure maintained within the identified to simulate an altitude betw~een ground level and 1 500 m. temperature shall be at least 25�C. An explosive mixture within be obtained by using the mixture~defined in 7.3 and 7.4.

Step

2 -

The internal case ignition source shall be energized in order to cause an explosion The occurrence of an explosion within the case may be detected by within the case. use~of a thermocouple inserted in the case and connnected to a sensitive galvanometer outside the test chamber. If ignition of the mixture does not occur immediately, the test shall be considered void and shall be repeated with a new explosive charge. At least five internal case explosions shall be performed. If the case tested is small (not in excess of l/150 of the test chamber volume) and if the reaction within the case upon ignition is of an explosive nature without continued burning of the mixture as it circulates into the case, more than one internal case explosion, but not more than five, may be produced without recharging the entire chamber. Ample time shall be allowed between internal case explosions for replacement of burnt gases with fresh explosive mixture within the case. If the internal case explosions ~produced did not cause a main chamber explosion, the explosiveness of the fuel-air mixture in the main If the air-vapour mixture in the main chamber is found not chamber shall be verified. to be explosive, the test shall be considered void and the entire procedure repeated. ca_uses a main be conducted. chamber explosion, the test

8.3.1 Procedure I ( Category El ) - Category El tests determine teristics of equipment not hermetically sealed and not contained in and explosion propagation. 8.3.1 .I Preparation for test

~a) The test item shall be connected and oriented mechanically and electrically as recommended This shall include any cooling by the manufacturer for normal service installation. provisions, as necessary to perform the tests described herein, and in such a ~manner so that normal electrical operation is possible and mechanlcal controls may be operated

External covers of the test item shall through the pressure seals from outside the chamber. be removed or loosened to facilitate the penetration of the explosive mixture. Large test items may be tested ( one or more units ) at a time by extending electrical connections through the cable port to the balance of the associated epuipment located externally.

b) 4

The test item shall be operated

to determine

that it is functioning

properly.

Mechanical loads on drive assemblies and servomechanical and electrical loads on switches and relays may be simulated if proper precaution is given to duplicating the normal load in respect In all instances, it is preferable to operate to torque, voltage, current, inductive reactance, etc. the test item as it normally functions in the installed environment.

8.3.1.2

Performance

of test pressures identified to simulate at maximum

The test shall be conducted between the ambient test altitude of 12 000 m above mean sea level. Step 1 -

The test chamber shall be sealed and the ambient temperature within shall be raised to 71�C. or to the maximum temperature at which the test item is designed to operate if lower than 71�C. The temperature of the test chamber and the chamber walls shall be permitted to rise to within 11�C of the chamber ambient air, prior to the introduction of the explosive mixture, to prevent condensation of the explosive medium. The required quantity of fuel ( see 7.4) shall be introduced into the chamber. 3 f 1 min shall be allowed for introduction and vapourization of the fuel within the chamber. At this time all electrical contacts of the test item shall be actuated. The operation of the test item shall be continuous throughout this period and all making and breaking electrical contacts shall be conducted as frequently as deemed practicable. If no explosion has occurred as a result of the test item operation, the potential explosiveness of the air-vapour mixture shall be verified by igniting a sample of the mixture with a spark gap or glow plug. If the air-vapour mixture is not found to be explosive, the test shall be considered void and the entire procedure repeated. If the item causes an explosion, it shall have failed the test and further

IO

IS : 8252 ( Part 21 ) - 1986 EXPLANATORY NOTE

This standard is a part of a series of Indian standards specifying similar environmental tests for aircraft equipment subjected to demonstrate that it would function satisfactorily under normal aircraft operating conditions. The relevant equipment specifications would define the appropriate test severities and criteria for correct functioning. This standard is based on the draft International Standard lSO/DlS 7137 `Aircraft - Environmental conditions and test procedures for air borne equipment', prepared by lSO/TC 20 the technical committee for aircraft and space vehicles. Other Indian Standards in this series to be formulated tests for aircraft equipment: General Temperatures, Ice formation pressure and humidity are:
